grounding.states: No single official 5-year fixed rate; it depends on the lender and on whether the mortgage is insured
grounding.from: No official, single "the" 5-year fixed rate exists. The figure depends on the lender and on whether the mortgage is insured (down payment under 20%) or uninsured.
Ratehub lists the best high-ratio (insured) 5-year fixed rate in Canada at 4.34%. Wowa gives the same 4.34% as the lowest insured 5-year fixed rate.

grounding.states: Rates have been climbing since early September
grounding.from: Rates are climbing in October 2026, after all six of the largest banks raised select fixed rates since early September.

grounding.states: One big bank is at 4.54% and Scotiabank at 4.74%
grounding.from: Ratehub's table (updated October 13) shows a Big 6 bank at 4.54% and Scotiabank at 4.74%.

grounding.states: No Toronto- or Ontario-specific rate found
grounding.from: The search results don't give a Toronto- or Ontario-specific rate.

grounding.states: Insured vs uninsured and new purchase vs renewal change the figure
grounding.from: I don't know whether the asker means an insured or uninsured mortgage, or a new purchase versus a renewal. That changes which figure applies.

value.answer: There's no single 5-year fixed rate, since each lender sets its own. The lowest insured one I found (down payment under 20%) is 4.34%, from Ratehub and Wowa. Big banks are higher: one is at 4.54% and Scotiabank at 4.74%. Rates have been climbing since early September. I didn't find a Toronto-specific number, and I can't tell whether you mean insured or uninsured, or a new purchase versus a renewal. That changes which rate applies.
